info.title: qe-report API
info.description: Transport API version 1 of qe-report. It is independent of the protocol version (0.3), the database schema version, the query-index version, and the package version. Every authenticated operation acts on the project its API key belongs to; no request names a project. Bearer API keys must only travel over HTTPS; TLS is expected at the deployment or reverse-proxy boundary.

post.summary: Upload one complete run as multipart protocol source and attachment bytes.

schema.description: The project is the API key’s; no part names one. Event streams are stored exactly as sent. Unknown part names are refused.

expiresAt.description: Required, exactly once, as text: the instant after which retention may delete the run. An RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset, seconds 00 to 59, and at most three fractional digits, so that it is exactly the millisecond it states. A leap second or a finer fraction is refused rather than read as an earlier instant. A past instant is valid and makes the run eligible at once.

events.description: One or more NDJSON protocol event streams, as file parts.

attachment.description: Zero or more attachment byte streams, as file parts, identified by the SHA-256 of their bytes; filenames and media types are ignored.

apiKey.description: A project-scoped API key, `qer_k1_<publicId>_<secret>`, issued by an operator. Its scope (runs:read or runs:write) is named by each operation in x-qe-report-scope.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Further members depend on the code: `diagnostics` and `runId` for a refused run, `totalRuns`, `missingRuns`, and `staleRuns` for an incomplete query index.

ProtocolComponent.description: A named, versioned piece of software: the adapter that produced the events, or the runner it observed.

ProtocolExecutor.description: The CI or local context that ran the session.

type.description: Runner-native classification, for example a Java exception class or an error name.

phase.description: Where the failure originated when the runner can tell: shared or per-test setup, the test body, or teardown.

ProtocolLocation.description: Where the test or step is defined, for display only. Never resolved on a server.

ProtocolPathSegment.description: One container in the runner's own hierarchy. Well-known kinds are 'file' and 'group'; a runner-specific kind (for example Playwright 'project') is permitted and treated like a group by consumers that do not know it.

ProtocolSource.description: Version control state of the tested code.

ProtocolStringMap.description: Key-value pairs with string values. Keys are bounded; at most 64 entries.

executionId.description: Identifies the logical test within this run. Every attempt of the same test in the run carries the same executionId.

historicalId.description: Identifies the same logical test across runs. Derived by the adapter. Required unless historicalIdStability is 'unavailable'.

historicalIdStability.description: stable: the adapter expects the historicalId to survive unrelated edits. uncertain: it is derived from positional information such as indexes or line numbers. unavailable: no historical identity can be given (for example a dynamically generated test).
